finding: The +120-second final-rearm canary has not demonstrated continuation or authority-safety benefit over the +60-second comparator. Its nominal idle cost is 60 seconds higher than +60 and 77.1 seconds above the P0 42.9-second average non-useful-gap budget before startup/provider costs. Timing accuracy is not a promotion argument because observed delivery jitter is bidirectional and mean absolute offset is 101 seconds.
decision: Do not promote +120 as the long-term utilization policy. The current bootstrap explicitly locks +120 for this run, so preserve it during this wake. On the next operator-authorized policy revision, prefer rollback to +60 unless new evidence demonstrates a measurable continuation or authority-safety benefit that offsets the extra nominal idle minute.
